title: Hemin suppresses interferon responses in periodontal cell models through JAK2-STAT1 inhibition.
authors: Huang, Xiaoyu; Gruber, Reinhard; Panahipour, Layla
one_liner_zh: 该文研究血红素通过JAK2-STAT1抑制干扰素应答，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA体系，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Hemin, an oxidized heme species released during erythrocyte breakdown, is detectable in gingival crevicular fluid during periodontal inflammation, but its effects on local immune signaling remain unclear. We investigated whether hemin modifies cytokine-induced interferon responses in HSC-2 oral squamous cell carcinoma cells and primary human gingival fibroblasts. METHODS: Cells were stimulated with interleukin-1beta and tumor necrosis factor-alpha, or with interferon-gamma, in the presence or absence of hemin. Transcriptomic changes were assessed by RNA sequencing and pathway analysis, and selected transcripts and proteins were validated by reverse-transcription quantitative PCR, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, immunoblotting, and immunofluorescence. Ligand-kinase interactions were examined by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations, and recombinant Janus kinase 2 activity was measured in a cell-free assay. RESULTS: Hemin preferentially suppressed an interferon-associated gene network, including CXCL10, CXCL11, MX1, OAS1, IFIT1, IFIT3, and ISG15, while nuclear factor kappaB-associated responses were comparatively preserved. Hemin also reduced signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 Tyr701 phosphorylation and nuclear accumulation induced by either the cytokine combination or interferon-gamma. Computational analyses predicted stable hemin interactions within conserved ATP-binding pockets of Janus kinases, and the cell-free assay demonstrated inhibition of recombinant Janus kinase 2. DISCUSSION: Together, these findings show that hemin attenuates interferon-associated transcription in periodontal cell models, consistent with inhibition of the Janus kinase 2-signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 axis. This mechanism may enable blood-derived hemin to modify local mucosal immune signaling, although its relevance to periodontal tissues and antiviral defense requires confirmation in organotypic, infection, and in vivo models.
abstract_zh: 引言：血红素（hemin）是红细胞分解过程中释放的一种氧化型血红素物种，在牙周炎症期间可在龈沟液中检测到，但其对局部免疫信号传导的影响仍不清楚。我们研究了血红素是否修饰HSC-2口腔鳞状细胞癌细胞和原代人牙龈成纤维细胞中细胞因子诱导的干扰素反应。方法：细胞在存在或不存在血红素的情况下，用白细胞介素-1β和肿瘤坏死因子-α，或干扰素-γ进行刺激。通过RNA测序和通路分析评估转录组变化，并通过逆转录定量PCR、酶联免疫吸附测定、免疫印迹和免疫荧光验证选定的转录本和蛋白质。通过分子对接和分子动力学模拟检查配体-激酶相互作用，并在无细胞测定中测量重组Janus激酶2活性。结果：血红素优先抑制干扰素相关基因网络，包括CXCL10、CXCL11、MX1、OAS1、IFIT1、IFIT3和ISG15，而核因子κB相关反应相对保留。血红素还减少了由细胞因子组合或干扰素-γ诱导的信号转导子和转录激活子1 Tyr701磷酸化及核积累。计算分析预测血红素在Janus激酶保守ATP结合口袋内具有稳定相互作用，无细胞测定显示对重组Janus激酶2的抑制。讨论：综合这些发现表明，血红素在牙周细胞模型中减弱干扰素相关转录，与Janus激酶2-信号转导子和转录激活子1轴的抑制一致。这一机制可能使血液来源的血红素修饰局部黏膜免疫信号传导，但其对牙周组织和抗病毒防御的相关性需在器官型、感染和体内模型中确认。
